chunks: Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the children of the polytheists who die before reaching the age of responsibility. He said: "They are disbelievers, and Allah knows best what they would have done; they will enter the same places as their fathers."

key_terms.الْحِنْثَ: the age of moral responsibility or legal accountability
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: the polytheists; those who associate partners with Allah
key_terms.مَدَاخِلَ: places of entry or destinations entered

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the children of polytheists who die before reaching the age of responsibility?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the fate of the children of polytheists who die before reaching moral responsibility. It states that their outcome follows that of their fathers, while affirming that Allah knows best what they would have done. The narration relates to questions of divine knowledge, accountability, and the afterlife.
